partner_sact_assessed_separately.label: If combination therapy: partner SACT assessed separately

recent_major_surgery_or_unhealed_wound.label: Recent major surgery or unhealed wound

planned_major_surgery.label: Elective major surgery within the agreed withholding window (usually 28 days)

hypertension_grade.label: Hypertension grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No treatment-emergent hypertension.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Pre-hypertension range or transient mild elevation; no antihypertensive treatment indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Persistent or recurrent elevation requiring initiation or adjustment of one antihypertensive agent; generally 140–159/90–99 mmHg in adults.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe elevation requiring more than one drug or more intensive treatment; generally at least 160 systolic or 100 diastolic in adults.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences such as hypertensive crisis; urgent intervention required.

hypertension_grade.assessment_guidance: Use repeated, correctly measured blood pressure readings and record whether antihypertensive treatment or urgent intervention is required.
hypertension_grade.source_grading_note: NCCP v7 uses toxicity grades without specifying a CTCAE edition in this table; the existing CTCAE v5 interface aid must not replace clinician grading or independently define the source thresholds.

severe_bp_uncontrolled.label: Clinician confirms severe BP >200/110 mmHg remains uncontrolled with medication
severe_bp_uncontrolled.help: Source gives a paired BP value, not an explicit Boolean rule for isolated systolic/diastolic readings. Confirm measurement, symptoms and management; do not infer from one number.

urine_protein_g_24h.label: 24-hour urine protein
urine_protein_g_24h.help: Enter the current 24-hour total protein relevant to this assessment. It may resolve a preceding screening dipstick only when collected for that same episode; do not substitute an older result or a spot g/L concentration.

fistula_grade.label: Fistula grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No fistula. Use the anatomical site-specific CTCAE fistula term.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Asymptomatic; clinical or diagnostic observations only.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Symptomatic; non-invasive intervention indicated.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe symptoms; invasive intervention indicated.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

fistula_grade.assessment_guidance: Use the anatomical site-specific CTCAE fistula term; assess symptoms, need for invasive intervention and life-threatening consequences.
fistula_grade.source_grading_note: NCCP v7 uses toxicity grades without specifying a CTCAE edition in this table; the existing CTCAE v5 interface aid must not replace clinician grading or independently define the source thresholds.

thromboembolic_event_grade.label: Thromboembolic event grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No thromboembolic event.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Grade 1 is generally not used for clinically confirmed venous or arterial thromboembolism; use the specific CTCAE term.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Medical intervention such as anticoagulation is indicated without urgent instability.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Urgent medical intervention or hospital care is indicated.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening haemodynamic or neurological consequences; urgent intervention required.

thromboembolic_event_grade.assessment_guidance: Confirm the event and assess symptoms, need for anticoagulation or urgent intervention, hospitalisation, haemodynamic or neurological instability.
thromboembolic_event_grade.source_grading_note: NCCP v7 uses toxicity grades without specifying a CTCAE edition in this table; the existing CTCAE v5 interface aid must not replace clinician grading or independently define the source thresholds.

haemorrhage_grade.label: Haemorrhage grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No bleeding. Select the anatomical site-specific CTCAE haemorrhage term.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Mild bleeding for which intervention is not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Moderate bleeding requiring medical treatment or minor intervention.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe bleeding requiring transfusion, invasive intervention or hospital care.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening bleeding with urgent intervention required.

haemorrhage_grade.assessment_guidance: Grade using the site-specific CTCAE haemorrhage term, intervention required, transfusion need, hospitalisation and haemodynamic consequences.
haemorrhage_grade.source_grading_note: NCCP v7 uses toxicity grades without specifying a CTCAE edition in this table; the existing CTCAE v5 interface aid must not replace clinician grading or independently define the source thresholds.

renal_or_hepatic_clinical_concern.label: Renal or hepatic abnormality requiring clinical review

planned_minor_surgery.label: Minor surgery within the agreed withholding window (usually 7 days)

breast_her2_negative.label: For breast indication: HER2-negative disease confirmed

summary: Bevacizumab component has minimal emetogenic potential; no routine antiemetic prophylaxis is required for bevacizumab alone. Companion chemotherapy must receive its own assessed support plan.
Premedication is not usually required unless previous hypersensitivity; anti-diarrhoeal treatment may be required under local policy.
Check BP before each cycle and after treatment, urine protein, FBC, renal and liver profile; review bleeding, thrombosis, wounds and perforation risk.
Warfarin: INR weekly until stable, then before each cycle. Consider baseline echocardiography after anthracycline or chest-wall radiotherapy; NCCP does not specify a fixed repeat-echo interval.
supportive_care.mapping_basis: Highest active parenteral component is minimal emetogenic risk in NCCP V6 Table 7.

baseline: Urinalysis for protein and blood pressure
Cardiac history/examination; consider ECHO after prior anthracycline or chest-wall radiotherapy
before_each_cycle: Urinalysis for protein; quantify when indicated
Blood pressure before each cycle and post-treatment
ongoing: Warfarin INR weekly until stable, then before each cycle
BP more frequently if hypertension develops/worsens
Disease monitoring according to the individual treatment plan
